items.title: Disadvantage gap in England
items.claim: England's 'disadvantage gap' tracks attainment of pupils eligible for free school meals against peers. After narrowing in the 2010s, what happened from 2019?

options.text: It widened, including after pandemic disruption
It reversed: FSM pupils overtook peers

items.reveal:
Education Policy Institute analyses reported the disadvantage gap at GCSE widened from 2019, reaching its widest in over a decade by 2022.

Pandemic-related school closures appear to have amplified pre-existing trends.
items.why: Apparent progress can reverse when systems are stressed, revealing structural fragility.

items.title: Oakley's domestic labour finding
items.claim: Ann Oakley's The Sociology of Housework (1974) interviewed 40 London housewives. What did most report about housework?

options.text: It was monotonous, low-status and isolating
It was equally shared with husbands
It was paid at market rates

items.reveal:
Oakley reported 70% of respondents expressed dissatisfaction. Her work established housework as a legitimate object of sociological study.

Later 'second shift' research (Hochschild, 1989) extended the analysis to employed women.
items.why: Recognising unpaid labour as work reframed measurements of economic activity.
